title: An Intelligent Surveillance Platform for Large Metropolitan Areas with Dense Sensor Deployment
thesis: A technical description of an intelligent video surveillance platform using low-cost sensors and multiple AI engines for autonomous alarm detection in urban environments.
theme_1_justification: Not addressed. The paper focuses on technical implementation of a surveillance system without discussing dual-use or technology transfer.
theme_2_justification: Not addressed. No discussion of algorithmic opacity, epistemic authority, or surveillance as knowledge production beyond technical functionality.
theme_3_justification: Not addressed. The paper describes a surveillance system but does not engage with concepts of machinic city or modulation of urban populations as a mode of governance.
theme_4_justification: Not addressed. No discussion of spatial destruction, home unmaking, or weaponization of infrastructure.
key_quotes: This paper presents an intelligent surveillance platform based on the usage of large numbers of inexpensive sensors designed and developed inside the European Eureka Celtic project HuSIMS.

The fact that the system is using low resolution visual sensors provides an additional advantage regarding governance and politics: the provided image does not usually allow recognition of people’s faces, which makes the system more respectful of privacy.
HuSIMS' main target is to provide real-time alerts for irregular activity in both indoors and outdoors scenarios.
notes: Technical paper; no engagement with dual-use or critical perspectives on algorithmic governance.
